US Oil: Synopsis of trade.

** This is a simulation trade from 1 year ago

Price breaks a previous support area on a 30-min chart.

There is a IQM on this TF. Need to zoom in on the area in the black box to look for LTF confirmation

1-min chart shows a confirming IQM on the 1-min chart. This is a very good sign. Black line is copied over from the previous chart, and the red line shows the LTF IQM.

Entry set at the black/red line, with the target located far enough from the entry to allow for a 4X RR. Stop loss is located just beyond the 30-min candle that crosses the black line (I will show that in greater detail next).

The stop loss is determined by looking at the HTF 'kink'. I am interested in the range for the candle that crosses the HTF IQM line. The range of the candle crossing this line changes depending on the scale used. I look at every scale...starting at the 1-min chart and going up to the 30-min chart. My stop loss is placed beyond the range of the 30-min candle that crosses the black HTF IQM line. See chart below:

My target was set based on two major considerations

1. I required a minimum3X RR or I wasn't going to take the trade.

2. I look for obvious problem areas where price may encounter a change in order flow. In this case, I saw the most recent demand zone (in this scale) that preceded price's bullish move to the area of my entry. Since I was short, this demand area (see yellow box in chart below) looked like the first major hurdle for shorts, as there is a high likelihood that ample buy orders exist at this demand area (change in order flow). I closed the position at the very top of this demand zone. Chart below:

Simulation on AUD-USD:

I used a free version of simulation software from FXCM, and it is useful but has a lot of bugs. One of the bugs happens when my entry order doesn't get triggered despite getting reached. That happened in this scenario, but I wanted to show the top down analysis of the trade anyway..it is a great example.

Like my oil trade above, I began by finding a HTF IQM.

Next, drop down to LTF and look for another IQM or other important PA that supports a possible long trade.

My main focus at this point is setting up the best trade with the lowest risk and highest return. I look at the last candle to cross the HTF IQM and I draw the range of that candle. As you can see from the chart below, the candle has a large range (44 pips). I look at every scale from 1-min to 30-min to draw a conservative candle...I place my stop loss just below the low of the candle on the 30 min scale... (In this example, the 30-min candle's low and the 1-min candle's low is the same)

The ideal place to go long is at the yellow shaded area where the black and red horizontal lines exist. But here is where MM and trade psychology comes in: I have to be aware of the necessary location of my stop loss. This stop loss has to be located below the low of the black box - and if I set an entry order to buy at the yellow shaded region, my SL is approximately 20 pips. This is too wide of a stop loss for my trading strategy. I am looking for a minimum 1:3 RR - but would rather see closer to 1:4 RR. In keeping consistent with my MM goal, an entry at the yellow zone requires a target to be located 60-80 pips from my entry - too ambitious. I want low risk high return trades. The only way to manage this trade properly (under my MM requirements) is to set my entry order no more than 11 pips from the SL. I do this specifically because my target for this trade is approx 35 pips away from the proposed entry. I accept the possibility that price will bounce at the yellow zone and leave me in the dust. I am OK with missing out on trades.

An important point regarding the target: I don't know my target until price unfolds and comes very close to my entry point. This can be complicated, since the entry is dependent on the SL but the SL is somewhat dependent on my proposed target. This is why it is important to watch trades as they unfold as opposed to setting a limit order and walking away. As price unfolds, I see a nice supply zone forming just before price takes a dive to my entry.

The chart below shows where my entry, SL, and target is located. As you can see, my simulation software didn't trigger like it should have..that said, it is easy to see how the trade would have turned out.

I know the entry above looks too good to be true...It is my humble opinion that predicting exact areas where price will turn is not always possible. I simply got lucky on this entry...price could have easily missed my entry by a couple of pips and there are times when this happens. In my opinion, this is why trading psychology is so important: the fear of missing out on a trade shouldn't cause a trader to execute a trade that is beyond the scope of their MM requirements. It takes practice but over time a trader can train themselves to shut off their emotions. I still struggle with this, but I am getting a lot better at it.

I currently have a buy order set for GBP-USD. Here is a top down analysis of the current setup.

HTF:

LTF confirmation of IQM. There are two areas of interest shown by yellow circles.

The range of the blue rectangle is too large...at approximately (21 pips). I need to reduce the risk, especially depending on where I expect the target to be located

My stop loss is shown on the chart below - the stop loss is located just beneath the low of the last 30 min candle to cross the HTF IQM line (black horizontal) and the LTF IQM (solid red line). Notes on the chart reiterate the issue with setting my entry order at the top of the yellow shaded rectangle.

The target (and the entry) is not set in stone at this point - the reason for this is I cannot set my entry unless I feel confident where my target is located, and I can't feel comfortable about the location of my target until I see more PA unfold. Specifically, I want to see PA as it approaches my entry. At this stage, I see the future downside break of the "FL" labeled on the chart below as the most likely area where my long position will encounter a substantial set of sell orders that could bounce price lower. Depending on how the PA develops as price approached my entry, the target may shorten. If so, my entry will likely be adjusted lower as well - to decrease the risk between my entry and the stop loss. My current entry order is set in an area that requires a 14-pip stop loss. This is a high stop loss for me - usually I like my stop loss to be at or under 10 pips. My requirement for a target is minimum 3X risk. In this case, the target is located approximately 64 pips from the entry (roughly 4.5 R). If my target drops, my entry will drop accordingly. My stop loss will not change.

A quick note regarding my methodology for entry (I am still in the process of refining my standard approach to setting an entry order): I understand price may bounce prior to price reaching my entry - in fact, this happens on a regular basis. I have decided to sacrifice good trading opportunities for a strict risk management plan. I am OK with missing out on trades but I am not OK with taking on too much risk Years ago I lost a very large live account over the course of a few short months. That is NEVER happening again. The main reason I don't adjust my positioning size instead (as opposed to adjusting my entry to control risk) is the issue of my target - wide stop losses require an equally wide target in order to meet my 3X risk/return requirement. My core specialty will be executing low risk short-term 'opportunity' trades. Once the SL exceeds 10 pips, my target requirement exceeds 30-40 pips, and it takes longer for the trade to complete, which exposes my trade to increased external risk.

EUR-JPY: A good example of a trade last week that I missed by about 5 pips: It's Important to remember to delete entry orders if price bounces prior to reaching the point of entry. In this case, price bounced with strength and reached the target without first reaching my entry.

I will delete my entry even if price does not fully reach its target. If there is a substantial reaction prior to my entry (but in close proximity to my entry, within the scope of my trade) I am not willing to wait in hopes of there being enough LQ bounce price again. I'd rather delete my entry order and look for another opportunity.

First trade was NZD-JPY short:

Practicing trading LS kinks... using simulation software from FXCM. It's free to use if you sign up for a demo account with them.

Here is a nice LS, with a kink (not visible on the hourly chart) but easily visible on the 1-min chart. The SL was 7 pips, the target was 70 pips (10:R).

The target was a QM level below...

I have been spending time trying to refine my understanding of kinks. Some hold, and some do not. Managing risk is critical.

Here is a trade I took on a demo account on NZD-USD: Here are the following points to my analysis:

1. Blue Rectangle = LS 2. Black Rectangle = HH & LL 3. Red Rectangle = the kink formed when price broke out of the LS (blue rectangle). 4. Price makes a new high and returns back to the red kink.

** The red kink is far too wide for an entry at the mouth. Instead, I went to a lower time frame and drew the inner Kink (gray box). This is a much tighter kink, and my entry was at this gray box. My FL was located just beyond the gray box (technically, it should have been below the red box) but this is how I manage the risk.
